methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capacity-building outside traditional tech hubs, testing whether peer-to-peer knowledge transfer can distribute deep literacy beyond NoVA's concentrated resources.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab creates a regional node of professional AI training, but its campus-based delivery model may deepen capability within existing professional networks rather than distributing to broader Appalachian communities facing economic transition.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community impact and education infrastructure, positioning Richmond as a potential distribution hub that could bridge the NoVA-rest-of-state divide through institutional knowledge transfer.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's policy incoherence—promoting AI while blocking the data centers that enable it—signals institutional fragmentation that could leave the state with neither deep capability nor broad distribution as communities reject infrastructure without gaining competency.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates concentrated demand for shallow platform skills rather than deep technical capability, signaling potential metro-hub adoption without the distributed peer networks needed for sustainable capacity-building.
